title: Audit lane demultiplexer and tenant-aware retention quotas
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As RBAC v2 expands roles and admin controls, audit traffic patterns are increasingly skewed by small numbers of high-activity tenants and admin automation (SSO/SAML flows, bulk admin actions). Our current ingest pipeline bundles all audit events into a single hot shard path which causes write hotspots, expensive long-term indexes, and unpredictable retention costs. This ticket proposes a lane demultiplexer at the ingestion edge plus tenant-aware retention quotas and index compaction profiles to: reduce hotspotting, make retention cost predictable per-tenant, and enable admin-scoped audit lanes (high-fidelity short-term vs. compacted long-term).

Goals:
- Demultiplex incoming audit streams into lanes: admin-actions, auth-events (SSO/SAML), tenant-ops, system-heartbeat.
- Route lanes to different indexing/partitioning profiles (e.g., admin-actions -> 7d hot index then compact, auth-events -> 30d hot then cold).
- Enforce tenant-specific retention quotas and soft-cost limits (per-tenant budget that triggers compaction/archival).
- Integrate RBAC v2 mappings so admin-scoped events are tagged and routed to high-fidelity lanes.
- Provide operator controls in Console to adjust lane mappings, quotas, and emergency retention overrides.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingest edge demultiplexer exists and can classify >=95% of audit events into the defined lanes with <500ms additional latency. 2) Tenant-aware retention quotas are enforced: when tenant budget breached, older indices are auto-compacted and a retention alert is emitted. 3) Admin lane preserves full fidelity for 7 days and then compacts to size-reduced index for 90+ days. 4) Console UI exposes per-tenant quota and lane assignment with read/write ACLs tied to RBAC v2. 5) Integration tests and a canary load run show no write amplification >10% and overall storage cost reduction in pilot tenants by >=30%.
design_notes:
High-level approach:
- At the ingestion gateway, add a lightweight classifier using event metadata and RBAC v2 subject tags to assign a "lane" header. Classifier rules stored in a small feature flag table (mutable by Console).
- Lanes map to pipeline templates: each template configures: index shard key (time vs tenant), segment target size, compaction policy, TTL retention, and coldstore archival cadence.
- Tenant quotas stored in tenant config service; quota meter publishes to a quota-orchestrator that triggers compaction/archival jobs and emits events to Ops.
- Indexing: use tenant-prefixed index namespaces and a sharding strategy that includes tenant hash + time bucket to avoid single-tenant hotspots. Use dynamic shard sizing for admin lane (small shards, frequent roll-over) and larger shards for compacted lanes.
- Cost control: when tenant cost approaches quota, switch future events for that tenant into a compacting pipeline (reduced index fields, coalesced events) and throttle non-critical telemetry writes.

Trade-offs considered:
- Classification accuracy vs latency: rule-based classifier chosen for predictable latency; ML classifier deferred to a follow-up.
- Per-tenant indices increase index count (meta overhead) but reduce cross-tenant noisy-neighbor effects. We'll cap per-tenant open index count via rollup.
- Emergency override allows admins to temporarily increase retention but requires audit and two-person approval (Console + API token).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): build classifier at ingest, implement lane header propagation, create pipeline templates for lanes, store lane mappings in config service. Phase 2 (2 sprints): implement tenant quota store and quota-orchestrator, wire compaction jobs, and add conservative compaction policy for admin lane. Phase 3 (1 sprint): Console controls for lane mapping and quotas, RBAC v2 ACL bindings, and canary rollout to 3 pilot tenants. Phase 4 (ongoing): tuning, metrics, and automation for auto-adjusting retention based on budget and SLOs.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for classifier rules and header propagation.
- Integration test harness that injects mixed traffic patterns (SSO events, bulk admin actions, normal tenant ops) to validate lane assignment.
- End-to-end load test with a pilot tenant at 10x expected peak to validate shard resilience and compaction behavior.
- Monitoring: new SLOs for ingest latency, lane misclassification rate, per-tenant storage growth, and cost-per-tenant.
- Security: verify RBAC v2 bindings prevent non-admins from changing lane mappings and ensure SSO/SAML event PII redaction is preserved before long-term storage.
observability_and_rollout:
- Add metrics: lane_count, lane_ingest_rps, lane_misclassification_rate, tenant_storage_bytes, tenant_quota_usage_percent.
- Dashboards: per-tenant storage trend, top-10 tenants by cost, lane-specific latency.
- Alerting: tenant_quota_usage > 90% (warning), >100% (action - auto-compaction trigger).
- Rollout plan: feature-flag the demultiplexer, enable for internal tenants first, then opt-in pilot customers (3 tenants), ramp to 20% traffic, then global.
- Rollback: feature-flag off restores previous single-lane pipeline; compaction reversal is not automatic (requires reindexing), so we document rollback implications in runbook.
